records.name: Mayfair Holmesburg Parade Committee
records.summary: The volunteer committee that puts on the Mayfair and Holmesburg Thanksgiving Parade each November. Neighbors can carry a banner, march, or enter a homemade float.
records.what_you_do: Carry a banner (7th grade and older; banner carriers earn 6 community service hours), apply to march in the parade, or build a homemade float and enter it for a best-float ribbon.

schedule.text: Parade on a Sunday in late November, 12 to 3 pm (2026 parade: November 22). The page asks for replies by November 13, 2026.

cost.text: No fee is named on the parade page.

first_step.how: Email info@thanksgivingparade.org to sign up as a banner carrier, or send the marching application (a PDF on the site) by email.
first_step.basis: Anyone can apply by email to march, carry a banner, or enter a float, but the page shows no beginner program or orientation.

records.notes: Borderline verdict: the committee runs one annual parade, so a reviewer may prefer not_a_group. Published as a program because volunteer roles open each year. The page names only the committee and the info email; no phone and no sign up form. The page shows the 49th annual parade on November 22, 2026. Mayfair and Holmesburg are placed in North Delaware by data/vocab/neighborhoods.yaml, not Lower Far Northeast as the slice lists them.

notes: Budget: all 6 WebSearch calls were used, and the search results were mostly 2009 to 2019 articles, so this is a thin run. Only 1 record was written (verdicts: publish 1; hide 0; not_a_group 0; duplicate 0; out_of_area 0). Blocked sources: Northeast Times returned 403 on every page tried (5 pages), so its 2022 and 2025 community roundups and its group notices were not read; it is the best local list source and needs a route the owner approves or a later run. The holmesburg.com civic site gave a TLS error twice. Two Free Library branch paths returned 403; I guessed those paths, and they are not from a search result. The philadelphianeighborhoods.com tag page returned 403. Not established: no Winchester Park or Pennypack Woods group was found; no Ashton-Woodenbridge civic association was found; no Council District 6 or 10 civic list page was found; I could not confirm District 10 for any group. A 2025 Water Department newsletter snippet places Holmesburg in District 6. The Mayfair Town Watch restart (a 2011 WHYY article, organizing meeting January 2012) and the Holmesburg civic notices (a 2009 WHYY article) are too old to show activity, so they are not recorded. The Pennypack Environmental Center volunteer garden group was mentioned in a search summary (2024 listing), but the phila.gov page I fetched did not show it, so it is not recorded. Friends of Poquessing Watershed runs cleanups near Torresdale (2019 search summary), but no own site was found and part of its work may be in Bucks County. Unverified, from background knowledge and needing a check: Pennypack Ecological Restoration Trust (PERT). Vocabulary: neighborhoods.yaml places Holmesburg, Mayfair and Torresdale in North Delaware, and Aston-Woodbridge is spelled aston_woodbridge there. Next run should retry holmesburg.com, look for the Council District 6 and 10 civic list pages, check the East Torresdale and West Torresdale/Morrell Park civic sites, and find the Mayfair Business Association's own site.
